name: agy-powerline-setup
description: Install or update the agy-powerline statusline and wire it into agy's settings. Use when the user asks to set up, install, update, fix or check agy-powerline.

findings.excerpt: 2. Run `npx -y agy-powerline@latest init --yes`. It installs the statusline in `~/.agy-powerline` and sets `statusLine` in agy's `settings.json`, after backing
- If npx can't download the package (a network, proxy or registry error such as `ENOTFOUND`, `ETIMEDOUT`, `ECONNREFUSED` or `E403`, not an error printed by `ini
3. Run `npx agy-powerline doctor` and sum up its result in two or three lines: whether the statusline command ran, and any problem it lists with the fix it sugg
5. Tell the user they can pick widgets, a theme and a layout with the `agy-powerline-customize` skill, or by running `npx agy-powerline configure` in their own
- Never run `npx agy-powerline configure`: it's an interactive full-screen editor and would hang your shell tool. Suggest it to the user instead.
- Never pass `--allow-exec` to `npx agy-powerline import` unless the user said yes to the exact commands `import` showed.
- If `init` itself fails, show its error message as printed and don't try to work around it (for example by writing files yourself). `npx agy-powerline doctor`
